name: microprediction
what_it_holds: "If you can measure it, consider it predicted" — an open, crowd-sourced real-time prediction/nowcasting platform and Python client where any published time series (economic, web-traffic, etc.) can be nowcast by a community of algorithms; includes APIs to pull live crowd-nowcasts of arbitrary streams.
why_useful: Not a data source itself, but a live nowcasting-as-a-service platform (gap #17, tangential to #4 point-in-time forecasts) — could in principle host or query a crowd-nowcast of a published economic series relevant to consumer/travel demand; more a curiosity than a direct fit, low priority.
themes: Nowcasting methods and packages: MIDAS, dynamic factor models, bridge equations, nowcasting with Google Trends, KPI nowcasting for companies
why_all: Not a data source itself, but a live nowcasting-as-a-service platform (gap #17, tangential to #4 point-in-time forecasts) — could in principle host or query a crowd-nowcast of a published economic series relevant to consumer/travel demand; more a curiosity than a direct fit, low priority.

name: scalecast
what_it_holds: General-purpose Python time-series forecasting library ('the practitioner's forecasting library') wrapping ARIMA, Prophet, LSTM, XGBoost, scikit-learn models with a unified pipeline for transformations, missing-value handling, and model stacking. 598 commits, MIT license. Does not implement MIDAS or mixed-frequency nowcasting specifically.
why_useful: Not a nowcasting-specific tool but a mature stacking/pipeline framework that could host whichever mixed-frequency model (MIDAS/DFM/LSTM) the team settles on for KPI nowcasting; low priority relative to the purpose-built packages above.
themes: Nowcasting methods and packages: MIDAS, dynamic factor models, bridge equations, nowcasting with Google Trends, KPI nowcasting for companies
why_all: Not a nowcasting-specific tool but a mature stacking/pipeline framework that could host whichever mixed-frequency model (MIDAS/DFM/LSTM) the team settles on for KPI nowcasting; low priority relative to the purpose-built packages above.

name: wayback_scraper (rockhazard)
what_it_holds: Python tool to download and reconstruct entire archived websites from the Wayback Machine (fetches all resources for a given URL/date range), MIT licensed, updated Jul 2026, 1 star. No data committed, generic.
why_useful: Same acquisition-method use case as waybackpy but page-reconstruction rather than API querying -- would let a researcher pull a full archived AirDNA or Mashvisor city-report page (not just text) for manual reading. Very small/low-maturity repo (1 star), unclear reliability.
themes: Wayback Machine / Internet Archive tooling and archived-page datasets (archived airbnb.com pages, archived AirDNA/Mashvisor market pages, archived Inside Airbnb site)
why_all: Same acquisition-method use case as waybackpy but page-reconstruction rather than API querying -- would let a researcher pull a full archived AirDNA or Mashvisor city-report page (not just text) for manual reading. Very small/low-maturity repo (1 star), unclear reliability.

name: Wayback-Scraper (KernelEquinox)
what_it_holds: Python script for quick enumeration of all archived snapshots of a given URL/domain via the Wayback CDX index. 9 stars, no license declared, no bundled data.
why_useful: Same generic-tooling use case; could be run against airbnb.com or AirDNA domains to enumerate which historical dates are archived before deciding whether a targeted pull is worth a human ask under rule 6.
